_schema.description: Candidate profiles, keyed by candidate id ('<district or region id>/<slug of Given Surname>', App.candidateId: the seat the person is contesting). Researched by hand from public sources and written in our own words: facts only, no commentary, nothing guessed. Every fact cites one or more entries in its profile's sources list by number. Anything a source states but we couldn't confirm carries unverified: true and a note. Rules: CLAUDE.md, 'Candidate profiles'.

fields.name: The candidate's name as the tracker lists it
fields.summary: {text, src}: 2-4 sentences in our own words; never text copied from a source
fields.born: {year, src, unverified?, note?} or null: year of birth only, and only if published (e.g. Wikipedia, Parliament of Victoria)
fields.lives: {place, src, unverified?, note?} or null: suburb or town only, and only if the candidate has stated it publicly
fields.occupation: {text, src, unverified?, note?} or null: current or most recent occupation outside politics, or 'Member of Parliament'
fields.prior_roles: [{role, kind (mp | minister | shadow | councillor | mayor | staffer | union | business | party | public-service | community | other), organisation?, from (year), to (year, or null if current), src, unverified?, note?}]
fields.previous_candidacies: [{election (e.g. '2022 Victorian state'), seat, party (code), result (Won | Lost | Retained | Withdrew | Unknown), src, unverified?, note?}]
fields.faction: {name, src, unverified?, note?} or null: only if reported by a mainstream news outlet or Wikipedia, citing that source
fields.priorities: [{text, quoted (true: the candidate's own words, under 15 words; false: our paraphrase), src}]: up to 5
fields.links: {website, party_page, abc, wikipedia, parliament, facebook, instagram, x, linkedin}: official pages and the candidate's own public accounts only; omit any that don't exist
fields.contact: {email: {value, kind (campaign | electorate office | party), src}, phone: {value, kind (party office | electorate office | campaign), src}}: published office or campaign contacts only; never personal numbers or addresses
fields.sources: [{id (number), url, title, accessed (YYYY-MM-DD)}]: every page a fact comes from
fields.profile_updated: YYYY-MM-DD when the profile was last researched

summary.text: Nina Taylor is the Labor member for Albert Park in the Legislative Assembly, first elected to that seat in 2022. From 2018 to 2022 she sat in the Legislative Council for Southern Metropolitan Region, where she was Government Whip. She has been Cabinet Secretary since August 2026 and is recontesting Albert Park in 2026.

occupation.text: Union organiser (Community and Public Sector Union); earlier a school teacher

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Training and Skills
Government Whip in the Legislative Council

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia doesn't say what label she stood under at this council election; the code is her party membership.

priorities.text: Better transport choices across several modes
Fair access to education and training pathways

summary.text: Matt Fregon is a Labor MP who won Mount Waverley in 2018 and has represented Ashwood since that district was created in 2022. He has been Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly since December 2022. He is standing again in Ashwood in 2026.

occupation.text: Owner and manager of a small IT business

prior_roles.role: Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
Deputy Government Whip in the Assembly

summary.text: Alison Marchant has been the Labor member for Bellarine since the 2022 election, when she succeeded the retiring Lisa Neville. Raised on a farm at Leopold, she taught in primary schools and campaigned against fracking before entering Parliament. She is seeking re-election in Bellarine in 2026.

occupation.text: Primary school teacher; later an electorate officer

priorities.text: Putting the community at the centre of government decisions

summary.text: Nick Staikos has held Bentleigh for Labor since 2014. He became a minister in December 2024 and since August 2026 has held the housing, building and precincts portfolio along with homelessness and seniors. He is recontesting Bentleigh in 2026.

occupation.text: Staffer to state and federal MPs

Minister for Housing, Building and Precincts

summary.text: Brad Battin is the Liberal member for Berwick, which he has held since 2022 after representing Gembrook from 2010 until that seat was abolished. He was Leader of the Liberal Party and Leader of the Opposition from December 2024 until a party-room spill in November 2025. He has since been shadow minister for police and corrections, and is standing again in Berwick in 2026.

occupation.text: Police officer, then owner of a bakery franchise

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Police and Corrections
Leader of the Victorian Liberal Party
Owner, Bakers Delight franchise in Wheelers Hill

faction.name: Liberal conservative
faction.note: Wikipedia says he is regarded as factionally conservative, but also reports that he has rejected that label.

summary.text: Paul Hamer won Box Hill for Labor in 2018 and has held it since. He joined cabinet in April 2026 and has been Minister for Roads and Road Safety since August 2026. He is recontesting Box Hill in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Roads and Road Safety

summary.text: James Newbury has been the Liberal member for Brighton since 2018. He was Shadow Treasurer from January to October 2025 and is now Shadow Attorney-General and Manager of Opposition Business. He is seeking re-election in Brighton in 2026.

occupation.text: Company secretary in financial services and political adviser

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Environment and Climate Change
prior_roles.note: Parliament gives the start as February 2022; Wikipedia gives September 2021.

prior_roles.role: Senior adviser to Premier Denis Napthine

faction.name: Liberal moderate
faction.note: Wikipedia calls him a moderate but also describes him as a close ally of a conservative-aligned group in the party.

priorities.text: A fair share of services and infrastructure for the area

summary.text: Kathleen Matthews-Ward has held Broadmeadows for Labor since 2022, when she succeeded the retiring Frank McGuire. She was earlier a City of Moreland councillor from 2004 to 2012 and worked as a policy adviser. She is recontesting Broadmeadows in 2026.

occupation.text: Policy adviser on disability, ageing and carers

prior_roles.role: Policy adviser (disability, ageing, carers and volunteers)

summary.text: Matthew Guy is the Liberal member for Bulleen, which he has held since 2014 after eight years in the Legislative Council for Northern Metropolitan Region. He was Minister for Planning from 2010 to 2014 and led the Liberal Party in opposition twice, from 2014 to 2018 and from 2021 to 2022. He is now Shadow Minister for Public Transport and is standing again in Bulleen in 2026.

occupation.text: Political staffer and government relations manager

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Transition to Government
Shadow Minister for Ports and Freight
Minister for Multicultural Affairs and Citizenship

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia gives the start year only.

prior_roles.role: Chief of staff to Denis Napthine (Opposition Leader)
Director of research, office of Premier Jeff Kennett

summary.text: Colin Brooks has represented Bundoora for Labor since 2006. He was Speaker of the Legislative Assembly from 2017 to 2022, then joined the ministry, and has been Treasurer and Minister for Industrial Relations since August 2026. He is recontesting Bundoora in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Industry and Advanced Manufacturing
prior_roles.note: Parliament gives the start as December 2024; Wikipedia gives October 2023.

Minister for Child Protection and Family Services
Minister for Disability, Ageing and Carers

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia gives the start year only.

Upgrades to public transport and roads
